summary: Passage EVK50 (SC25 demo): 800 Gbps per fiber, 16-lambda BiDi NRZ 50G/lambda. 4.6 pJ/bit total wall-plug (2.6 pJ/bit photonics + Guide + ~2 pJ/bit XSR SerDes). BER < 10^-9, >1 km reach, polarisation-insensitive, 25–105 °C range.

Passage EVK100: 3.2 Tbps per fiber at 112G PAM4 (16 lambda). 1.9 pJ/bit reference value on the Passage product family page / ISES Korea 2025; the EVK100 technical-spec page also lists a conservative 3.2 pJ/bit point. Monolithic PIC: MRM modulators, TIAs, Tx drivers on single chip.
Passage L200: 32 Tbps optical I/O per chip (56G NRZ, 3D CoW, 320 SerDes). L200X: 64 Tbps at 112G PAM4. Both <5 pJ/bit. Bandwidth density >1.5 Tbps/mm. Targeted 2026.

Passage M1000 EVK: 114.6 Tbps total bi-directional bandwidth, 2.3 pJ/bit system-level efficiency including laser, 1024 SerDes lanes, 256 optical fibers, 4,000 mm² active interposer area, integrated solid-state OCS.
OCP CPO reference architecture initiative. Partners: Celestica, Corning, Dell, Flex, Foxconn, Hyve, Keysight, Qualcomm, Quanta. Standards: OIF, IEEE, OCP.
World-record 1.6 Tbps per fiber (Qualcomm 112G PAM4 SerDes + Passage L-Series). 8x more bandwidth per fiber than Near-Packaged Optics.
>60 % TCO savings and 3–7x training speedup for 4.7T-param MoE (256 experts, 8 active) over 576 XPUs using L-Series vs electrical. Roadmap: pluggables 17–20 pJ/bit → 3D CPO as low as 3 pJ/bit.

Google introduced Gemini 3 as its latest and most intelligent Gemini model family, with Gemini 3 Pro in preview across Gemini, AI Studio, Vertex AI, Search, and Antigravity. Public posts do not disclose parameter counts.

Gemini app release notes state that Gemini 3.1 Pro is rolling out globally with higher limits for Google AI Pro and Ultra plans. The notes identify advanced reasoning but do not publish architecture or parameter sizes.

Gemini 3 Flash is described as a speed-optimized Gemini 3 model. Google reported more than 1T API tokens/day after Gemini 3 launch, 30% fewer thinking tokens than 2.5 Pro on typical traffic, and 3x faster behavior than 2.5 Pro based on external benchmarking cited in the post.
Google released an updated Gemini 3 Deep Think mode for scientific, research, and engineering tasks; it emphasizes longer, more expensive reasoning. Public posts do not disclose model size.

PyTorch/XLA SPMD exposes mesh and partition specs; XLA transforms a single-device program into a partitioned program with collectives using sharding annotations. This motivates modeling compiler-visible dataflow choices, not just link swaps.

TPU7x/Ironwood is Google's latest Cloud TPU. A pod has 9216 chips, 2307 BF16 TFLOP/s/chip, 4614 FP8 TFLOP/s/chip, 192 GiB HBM/chip, 7380 GiB/s HBM bandwidth/chip, and 1200 GB/s bidirectional ICI/chip. Google states it is designed for dense and MoE models, pre-training, sampling, and decode-heavy inference.
TPU v5p: 8960 chips per pod; 459 TFLOPS/chip, 95 GiB HBM, 2575 GiB/s HBM BW, 1200 GB/s bidirectional ICI per chip, 3D torus; 4x4x4 and larger slices have full torus connectivity.

Google describes Ironwood as XLA/software co-designed. A 64-chip cube uses dense 3D torus ICI; cubes scale to 9216 chips through an OCS fabric with dynamic optical reconfiguration and 88473.6 Tbps aggregate superpod connectivity.

Ironwood (2025): 4614 TFLOPS/chip, 192 GB HBM, 7.4 TBps HBM BW. 4x4x4 torus building block; 6 cube faces × 16 ICI links each. 96 optical + 80 copper + 64 PCB ICI connections per rack. Rack power-cap SLO < 15 ms; burst TDP window = 100 ms.
Advanced-packaging comparison point requested by the project prompt: 3.5 Tbps one-way link bandwidth and 6 pJ/bit per network hop.
